titulo: Práctica de Science — Repaso completo (Quiz #1: Nervous, Digestive y Excretory Systems)

temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): Your body connects to the world through the sensory organs. Each sensory organ gathers specific kinds of information. The information is sent to your brain, which is the control center of the body. The brain interprets the information and then tells the body how to react.
  • Eye — allows us to see. Light enters through the pupil, a lens focuses it onto the back of the eye, and a nerve sends signals to the brain, which interprets them to form a visual image.
  • Ear — allows us to hear. Sound waves make the eardrum vibrate; the ear changes the vibrations into nerve signals; a nerve carries them to the brain, which interprets them as words, music, or sounds.
  • Tongue — the sense of taste. Taste buds send signals to the brain, which interprets them as sweet, salty, bitter, or sour.
  • Nose — detects smell. It picks up chemicals in the air and changes them into nerve signals sent to the brain.
  • Skin — the sense of touch, from nerve endings that feel pressure, pain, hot, and cold. Fingertips have more nerve endings than other body parts.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra situación (no es una de las variantes): cuando olés una flor, la nariz detecta los químicos en el aire y los convierte en una señal nerviosa. Esa señal viaja hasta el cerebro, que la interpreta como 'ese es el olor de una rosa'. Así funcionan TODOS los órganos de los sentidos: recogen información y se la mandan al cerebro para que la interprete.

temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): The nervous system sends messages throughout your body. Your brain is your body's most complex organ. It interprets the information it receives about conditions inside and outside the body. Then it sends messages telling the body how to respond, or react. The brain is made up of nerve cells. Nerve cells also carry messages through the spinal cord to and from all parts of the body.
  • Cerebrum — controls your thoughts, imagination, feelings, and voluntary muscle movement (helps you think, learn, and remember).
  • Brain stem — controls body functions such as breathing, heart rate, and swallowing (things you don't think about).
  • Cerebellum — controls balance and coordination (helps you balance and move smoothly).
  • Spinal cord — carries messages to and from the brain.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra situación (no es una de las variantes): cuando andás en bicicleta sin caerte, el cerebelo (cerebellum) es el que te ayuda a mantener el equilibrio y a mover el cuerpo con suavidad. Si en cambio estás resolviendo un problema de matemática en tu cabeza, el que trabaja es el cerebro (cerebrum), porque ahí ocurre el pensamiento.

temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): The brain and the spinal cord make up the central nervous system. The spinal cord is made up of a thick bundle of nerves. Messages to and from your brain travel through the nerves of your spinal cord. These nerves branch out to other parts of the body. Some of these nerves are motor nerves that carry messages from the brain to other parts of the body. Other nerves are sensory nerves that carry messages from sense organs and other body parts to the spinal cord.
Del resumen: The nervous system is like your body's messaging system. It helps you think, feel, move, and react! Its two main parts are: 1. Central Nervous System (CNS) — the brain and spinal cord. The brain is the boss, it tells your body what to do. The spinal cord is like a highway for messages. 2. Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) — made up of nerves that spread all over your body, and carry messages to and from the brain and spinal cord.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra situación (no es una de las variantes): si tocás algo muy caliente, un nervio sensorial (sensory nerve) manda esa información desde tu mano hacia la médula espinal y el cerebro. El cerebro decide que hay que apartar la mano, y esa orden viaja de vuelta por un nervio motor (motor nerve) hasta los músculos de tu brazo.

temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): The digestive system breaks down food into nutrients and other substances that the body can use. Cells use these substances for energy, growth, and repair. Food undergoes many changes as it passes through the digestive system. Digestion begins in the mouth, where your teeth tear and crush food. Saliva, the liquid in your mouth, begins to chemically break down some food.
  • Mouth — where digestion starts. Teeth chew, and saliva helps break down food.
  • Esophagus — a tube that carries food to your stomach.
  • Stomach — uses acids and muscles to break down food into smaller pieces.
  • Small intestine — most digestion occurs here; nutrients are absorbed from food.
  • Large intestine — absorbs water and makes waste ready to leave the body.
El liver breaks down fats (a tube connects the liver to the small intestine), y el pancreas produces a chemical that adjusts sugar levels in your body — ambos mandan químicos al intestino delgado para ayudar a digerir.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra comida (no es una de las variantes): cuando comés una manzana, primero los dientes la mastican en la boca y la saliva empieza a descomponerla. Después baja por el esófago hasta el estómago, donde los ácidos la siguen descomponiendo. Luego pasa al intestino delgado, donde se absorben los nutrientes, y lo que sobra va al intestino grueso, que absorbe el agua y forma el desecho.

temas.nombre: How Nutrients Get to Parts of the Body
temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): We often think of the stomach as the organ that digests our food. But the stomach is involved in the digestion of only certain kinds of food. Most digestion takes place in the small intestine. In addition to the digestive juices produced by the intestine, the liver and the pancreas send chemicals to the small intestine to break down food. The small fingerlike structures on the inside of the small intestine are called villi. Capillaries line the walls of villi. Food that is completely digested is absorbed through the walls of the villi into the capillaries. The capillaries connect, or attach, with larger blood vessels that carry nutrients to all parts of the body.
Dato curioso del libro: en Japón, las personas tienen bacterias en el sistema digestivo que las ayudan a digerir el alga marina (seaweed) — bacterias que no se encuentran en personas de Norteamérica. Los científicos piensan que esas bacterias entraron a los intestinos japoneses a lo largo de muchas generaciones, por comer alga marina en muchas comidas.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otro nutriente (no es una de las variantes): cuando comés arroz, una vez que llega al intestino delgado, los nutrientes del arroz ya digerido pasan a través de las paredes de las villi hacia los capilares. Esos capilares se conectan con vasos sanguíneos más grandes, que llevan esos nutrientes hasta, por ejemplo, los músculos de tus piernas.

temas.explicacion:
Del libro (literal): Cells absorb nutrients from the blood, but in return they produce wastes. These wastes are removed from the body by the excretory system. Several organs help with this process. They include the lungs, the liver, and the skin, but mostly the kidneys, the bladder, and the urethra.
  • Kidneys — a pair of bean-shaped organs that filter wastes from the blood. As blood passes through the kidneys, capillaries remove these wastes. The wastes combine with water to form urine.
  • Ureters — tubes that move urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
  • Bladder — a muscular sac that stores urine until it is released from the body.
  • Urethra — a small tube through which urine is released out of the body.
temas.microleccion: Ejemplo con otra idea (no es una de las variantes): pensá en los riñones como un filtro de agua para pecera. El filtro deja pasar el agua limpia y atrapa la suciedad. Los riñones hacen algo parecido con la sangre: la sangre entra sucia (con desechos), pasa por los riñones, y sale limpia — mientras que los desechos, mezclados con agua, se convierten en orina.
